subject.title: Feature: configurable LLM retry with backoff on transient errors (overloaded/529)

question: Should OpenClaw expose a configurable LLM provider retry/backoff policy now, and if so should it be provider-level, agent-level, or deferred behind the narrower same-model retry work?
rationale: The request is useful for stability, but it adds public config and can replay provider calls or delay fallback, so automation should not choose the API shape or default behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor provider-level opt-in retry
options.body: Proceed with a provider-scoped config only after the runtime retry loop, idempotency gates, fallback ordering, docs, and upgrade proof are all included.

options.title: Defer until retry-family PRs land
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers finish the narrower same-model retry and overload-cooldown decisions, then revisit the public config surface.

options.title: Reject public retry config
options.body: Close this direction if maintainers prefer fixed internal retry/fallback policy and do not want another operator-facing LLM retry knob.

recommendation.title: Sponsor provider-level opt-in retry
recommendation.body: Proceed with a provider-scoped config only after the runtime retry loop, idempotency gates, fallback ordering, docs, and upgrade proof are all included.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the active maintainer-labeled adjacent retry-family PR and are the best current routing candidate among the available evidence.
